business_problem: The challenge was not simply building more capable robots.
solution_summary: As labor shortages and aging populations in Japan drive demand for robotics in healthcare and services, organizations need systems that support workers. The challenge was not simply building more capable robots. Building on Azure, Kawasaki is currently developing a robotics as a service platform that decouples software from hardware, unifying AI, data, and operations to enable scalable deployment of intelligent robotics systems and lay the foundation for physical AI. With Kawasaki’s KARAKURI initiative, users without robotics expertise—including healthcare professionals—can build and operate robot applications using natural language instructions.

For Kawasaki, scaling meant more than expansion; it required a new operating model.
The model delivered powerful automation capabilities but made it difficult to scale innovation across industries and use cases.
Organizations were looking for new ways to automate repetitive work while enabling people to focus on higher-value tasks.
Kawasaki set out to develop a cloud-based robotics as a service platform capable of supporting repeatable, production-scale deployment of intelligent robotics systems.
The objective was clear: transform robotics from a series of engineering projects into a scalable business capability.
